thread:
sara: FYI — Acme just opened a ticket saying their org-level latency dashboard in EU is missing the 95th and 99th percentile curves for multiple services after the morning rollout. Screenshot attached: https://redwood-share/acme/ss1.png

sara: They still see avg and p50 lines, but the 95/99 rows are blank in the panel and the legend only shows p50/p90. Customer is on org id 7812. Escalating, assigning to eng. :exclamation:

ingrid: thanks — can you paste the dashboard permalink and the timeframe they used? also do we have the org id + example service name?

sara: permalink: https://console.redwood/boards/latency?org=7812&range=1h ; timeframe: last 1h ; example service: inventory-api.

sara: quick check i ran from our console (promql) — note the histogram_quantile query returns empty for 95/99:

```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{org="7812",service="inventory-api"}[5m])) by (le))
# -> no series returned
```

jay: pinging metrics team. we rolled a config flip to the EU ingest canary earlier today to reduce bucket cardinality; i wonder if that suppressed higher quantiles. Deploy record: deploy-bot: metrics-ingest-eu v3.4.0 -> prod-eu by @jay at 2392007200.

deploy-bot: metrics-ingest-eu v3.4.0 deployed to prod-eu (canary) by jay — changelist: telemetry: enable_quantile_suppression=true

ingrid: if the ingest pipeline now drops bucket series above a certain quantile or converts them to a precomputed summary that only exports p50/p90, histogram_quantile calls could return no data. can you check raw bucket series for that org? e.g. run: 

```
series = series(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{org="7812"})
# expected many series with `le` label per request latency bucket
```

sara: ran `series(...)` — still see raw buckets but labels look different: the service label is `svc` instead of `service` for the ingested series: `http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{org="7812",svc="inventory-api",le="0.1"}`. Dashboard panels are still grouping by `service`.

ingrid: aha. label-remap in the transform changed `service` -> `svc` for the EU canary. panels that `by (service)` won't match anymore, and our dashboard's histogram_quantile queries use `by (service)` which means aggregation returns nothing for those panels' expected grouping. That would hide p95/p99 curves while p50 (precomputed metric) still shows up if we kept an explicit `http_request_duration_seconds_p50` metric.

jay: confirmed — the canary included two changes: (1) quantile_suppression=true and (2) label_remap service->svc. The suppression removed some precomputed higher-quantile exports in the transform, and the label_remap broke group-by in many dashboards. My bad for rolling both in the same canary.

jay: mitigation options: (A) roll back the label_remap and re-enable full bucket export for orgs flagged as paying/enterprise, (B) update dashboards as a short-term fix to accept `svc` in queries (e.g. `by (svc)` or use `coalesce(service, svc)` in panel query if supported), or (C) re-run transform with mapping that preserves both labels.

ingrid: for immediate triage, can we re-run the transform in read-only mode for org 7812 to restore `service` label and keep quantile exports for that org? if not, roll back the canary to restore previous behavior.

jay: we can hotfix: flip label_remap off in canary and re-enable quantile exports for org 7812. i'll push a rollback toggle now and post status.

jay: rollback toggle applied to prod-eu canary at 2392009000 — re-enabled full bucket export and removed service->svc remap for orgs in the enterprise whitelist.

sara: customer confirmed: dashboard now shows 95th and 99th curves for inventory-api and other services in org 7812. they say things look back to normal. :white_check_mark:

ingrid: thanks all. follow-up actions: (1) metrics team to separate label remap and suppression into separate toggles and add automated dashboard compatibility tests, (2) product to review org-level whitelist rules before enabling quantile_suppression, (3) support to notify other customers potentially impacted by the EU canary. i'll open a P1 ticket to track.

sara: filing the customer follow-up and tagging acme. thanks!
